skills.title: Say skip-count sequences by 2s, 5s and 10s
Count a collection by making equal groups and skip counting
Continue a skip-count sequence from any start and fill missing numbers

expectations: Put things into equal groups of 2, 5 or 10
Say one number per group, jumping by the group size each time
Keep going from the last number said; never start again from 1
Count any leftovers on from the last number
The last number said tells how many there are in all

misconceptions.belief: When skip counting, loses track and counts the last group or the leftovers by ones starting again from 1
signs: Says "2, 4, 6, 8 … 1" and reports the leftover count as the total
Restarts at 1 halfway through a collection
Total comes out smaller than the number of groups times the group size

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya counts chappals: 2, 4, 6, 8, and then there is 1 more chappal. How many chappals are there?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya chappal gin rahi hai: 2, 4, 6, 8… aur ek chappal aur bachi hai. Toh total kitni chappal hui?

remediation.representation: Counters in pairs with a running-total card that changes after every group
remediation.moveShape: Child touches each group and says the running total aloud; at the leftover, ask what number we were on and count on from there

misconceptions.belief: Counts a leftover group that is not full as if it were a full group
signs: Adds 5 for a last group that has only 2 or 3 things
Total comes out a little too big
Does not check whether the last group is full

diagnostic.prompt_en: Shells are in groups of 5. There are 3 full groups and 2 more shells. Aman counts 5, 10, 15, 20. Is he right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Shells 5-5 ke group mein hain. 3 poore group hain aur 2 shells alag se. Aman ginta hai 5, 10, 15, 20. Kya woh sahi hai?

remediation.representation: Five-frames where the last frame shows empty slots
remediation.moveShape: Before counting the last group, ask the child to check if it is full; count only what is really there

misconceptions.belief: Believes counting by 2s or 5s gives a different total from counting one by one
signs: Recounts by ones "to be sure" and expects a different number
Gives the number of groups as the total
Surprised that both ways give the same answer

diagnostic.prompt_en: Meena counted 10 laddoos one by one. Raju counts the same laddoos by 2s. What will Raju get?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Meena ne 10 laddoo ek-ek karke gine. Raju wahi laddoo 2-2 karke ginega. Raju ko kitne milenge?

options.text: A different number, because he counted in a different way

remediation.representation: The same collection counted twice side by side: ones on top, pairs below
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts first, then counts both ways; ask why the number did not change

items.prompt_en: Count by 2s with me: 2, 4, 6, 8. What comes next?
items.prompt_hi: Chalo 2-2 karke ginte hain: 2, 4, 6, 8… ab aage kya aayega?
hints: What did we add each time?
We jump by 2 each time.
8 and 2 more is ___?
After 8 comes 10 when we count by 2s.

items.prompt_en: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, ___, 25. Which number is missing?
items.prompt_hi: 5-5 karke gino: 5, 10, 15, ___, 25. Beech mein kaunsa number gayab hai?
hints: What comes after 15?
We jump by 5 each time.
15 and 5 more is ___?
15 + 5 = 20, so 20 is missing.

items.prompt_en: There are 6 pairs of chappals at the beach. Count them by 2s. How many chappals?
items.prompt_hi: Beach pe chappal ke 6 jode hain. 2-2 karke gino. Kitni chappal hain?
hints: How many chappals are in one pair?
Say one number for each pair: 2, 4, …
Six pairs: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. So 12 chappals.

items.prompt_en: There are 4 hands. Each hand has 5 fingers. Count by 5s. How many fingers?
items.prompt_hi: 4 haath hain. Har haath mein 5 ungliyan. 5-5 karke gino, kitni ungliyan?
hints: How many fingers on one hand?
Say one number per hand, jumping by 5.

items.prompt_en: Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, ___, ___, 60. Which two numbers are missing?
items.prompt_hi: 10-10 karke gino: 10, 20, 30, ___, ___, 60. Kaunse do number gayab hain?
hints: What do we add each time here?
Each jump is 10.
30, then ___, then ___, then 60.
30, 40, 50, 60, so 40 and 50 are missing.

items.prompt_en: There are 10 shells. If we count them by 2s instead of one by one, will we get more, fewer, or the same number? Guess first, then we will count.
items.prompt_hi: Yahan 10 shells hain. Agar hum ek-ek ki jagah 2-2 karke ginein, toh number zyada aayega, kam aayega, ya utna hi? Pehle guess karo, phir ginenge.
hints: Will the shells change if we count differently?
Counting a new way does not add or remove shells.
Still 10. The way we count does not change how many there are.

verified.note: Key correct. Hint leak: hint 2 ('counting a new way does not add or remove shells') gives away 'same' before step 4.

items.prompt_en: You counted 7 pairs of socks and got 14. How do you know it is 14 socks and not 7?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne moze ke 7 jode gine aur 14 bola. Tumhe kaise pata ki 14 moze hain, 7 nahi?
items.answer: Each pair has 2 socks, so 7 groups of 2 make 14; 7 is the number of pairs, not socks
hints: What is in one pair?
Think: is 7 counting socks or pairs?
Each pair has ___ socks.
Seven pairs with 2 in each: 2, 4, … 14. Seven is how many pairs.

verified.solverAnswer: each pair has 2 socks; 7 pairs x 2 = 14

items.prompt_en: Box A has 3 full groups of 5 shells. Box B has 2 full groups of 5 and one group of only 3. Which box has more shells? How many in each?
items.prompt_hi: Box A mein 5-5 shells ke 3 poore group hain. Box B mein 5 ke 2 poore group aur ek group mein sirf 3. Kis box mein zyada shells hain? Dono mein kitne?
items.answer: Box A: A has 15, B has 13
hints: Are all the groups in Box B full?
Count the full groups by 5s, then add the small group by ones.

verified.solverAnswer: Box A has more: A 15, B 13

items.prompt_en: I counted shells by 10s: 10, 20, 30, and there were 3 more shells. So I said there are 3 shells. Did I count right? What should it be?
items.prompt_hi: Maine shells 10-10 karke gine: 10, 20, 30, aur 3 shells aur the. Toh maine bola 3 shells hain. Kya maine sahi gina? Sahi kya hoga?
hints: Where was I in the count before the 3 extra shells?
Keep going from 30, do not start again.
We were on 30, so 31, 32, 33. There are 33 shells.

items.prompt_en: A frog starts at 0 and jumps 10 each time on a number line. After 4 jumps, where is it? Now tell it with ₹10 notes: 4 notes of ₹10 make how much?
items.prompt_hi: Ek mendhak 0 se shuru karke number line pe har baar 10 kudta hai. 4 jump ke baad woh kahan hoga? Ab ₹10 ke notes se batao: ₹10 ke 4 note kitne hue?
hints: Where does the frog land after 1 jump?
Each jump is 10, and each note is ₹10 too.
4 jumps of 10 land on 40, and 4 notes of ₹10 make ₹40.

items.prompt_en: In a cricket match, Arjun ran 2 runs, 8 times. How many runs did he make?
items.prompt_hi: Cricket match mein Arjun ne 8 baar 2-2 run bhaage. Usne kitne run banaye?
hints: How many runs each time?
Count by 2s, once for each time he ran.

items.prompt_en: Golu has 8 pairs of bangles and wants to count them fast. Teach Golu how to count them by 2s, and tell him how many bangles there are.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ke paas chudiyon ke 8 jode hain aur woh jaldi ginna chahta hai. Golu ko sikhao 2-2 karke kaise ginte hain, aur batao kitni chudiyan hain.
items.answer: Make pairs, say one number per pair jumping by 2 (2, 4, 6 … 16), keep going without restarting; 16 bangles
hints: What would you tell Golu to do first?
Talk about the groups and the jumps.
For each pair, we say the next number: 2, 4, ___ …
Make pairs, jump by 2 for each pair: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. That is 16 bangles.

verified.solverAnswer: pair up, jump by 2 per pair to 16; 16 bangles

items.prompt_en: Quick! Count by 10s from 10 to 100.
items.prompt_hi: Jaldi se! 10 se 100 tak 10-10 karke gino.
acceptable: das, bees, tees, chaalees, pachaas, saath, sattar, assi, nabbe, sau
hints: How do we start?
Each number has one more ten.

verified.note: Key correct. Matcher risk: 'acceptable' is one comma-joined string, not a list of variants.

items.prompt_en: Count by 2s starting from 20: 20, 22, 24, ___, ___. What are the next two numbers?
items.prompt_hi: 20 se 2-2 karke gino: 20, 22, 24, ___, ___. Agle do number kya hain?
hints: What is 2 more than 24?
Keep jumping by 2.

workedExample.problem: How many chappals are there in 5 pairs?
steps: Each pair has 2 chappals.
Touch each pair and count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
The last number we say is how many in all.
5 pairs make 10 chappals.
fadedVersion: Each pair has ___ chappals.
Touch each pair and count by 2s: 2, 4, ___, 8, ___.
The last number we say is how many in ___.
5 pairs make ___ chappals.

skills.title: Make a sensible estimate of a collection using a known group as a guide
Check an estimate by grouping in 10s and counting
Judge whether an estimate is close to or far from the actual number

expectations: An estimate is a thinking guess made without counting every object
Use a group you know (like 10) to help guess
A good estimate is close to the real number; it does not have to be exact
Check by making groups of 10 and counting
Spreading things out or bunching them up does not change how many there are

misconceptions.belief: Believes an estimate is wrong unless it is exactly the real number
signs: Refuses to guess and insists on counting first
Says "I was wrong" when the guess was 30 and the count was 32
Rubs out the guess after counting

diagnostic.prompt_en: Tara guessed there were 30 peanuts. When she counted, there were 32. Was her guess a good guess?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tara ne guess kiya 30 moongphali. Ginne pe 32 niklin. Kya uska guess achha tha?

options.text: No, it was wrong because it is not 32

remediation.representation: A number line with the guess and the real count marked, showing how close they are
remediation.moveShape: Celebrate closeness: ask how far apart the two numbers are; call close guesses good thinking

misconceptions.belief: Judges how many by how much space the things take up, so a spread-out row seems to have more
signs: Says the longer row has more even with the same count
Changes the estimate when objects are moved apart
Guesses more for a pile of big things

diagnostic.prompt_en: Row A has 8 marbles close together. Row B has 8 marbles spread far apart. Which row has more marbles?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Row A mein 8 kanche paas-paas hain. Row B mein 8 kanche door-door hain. Kis row mein zyada kanche hain?

options.text: Row B, because it is longer
Row A, because it is crowded

remediation.representation: Match each marble in one row with one in the other using lines
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts, then pairs objects one-to-one; ask what changed and what did not

misconceptions.belief: Counts the number of groups as if each group were a single object
signs: Says 3 cones of 10 peanuts is "3"
Adds the number of groups to the leftovers (4 tens and 5 → 9)
Ignores how many are in each group

diagnostic.prompt_en: Peanuts are in 3 paper cones. Each cone has 10 peanuts. How many peanuts in all?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Moongphali 3 kaagaz ke cone mein hai. Har cone mein 10 moongphali. Total kitni?

remediation.representation: Ten-sticks that can be opened to show 10 single beads inside
remediation.moveShape: Open one group and count it, then count the groups by 10s

items.prompt_en: One handful has about 10 peanuts. Mummy puts 3 handfuls in a paper cone. About how many peanuts are in the cone?
items.prompt_hi: Ek mutthi mein lagbhag 10 moongphali aati hain. Mummy ne 3 mutthi cone mein daalin. Cone mein lagbhag kitni moongphali hongi?
hints: How many in one handful?
Count the handfuls by 10s.
Three handfuls of about 10 is about 30.

items.prompt_en: Let us check a guess. We made groups of 10 peanuts: 10, 20, 30, and 4 more are left. How many peanuts are there?
items.prompt_hi: Chalo guess check karte hain. 10-10 ke group banaye: 10, 20, 30, aur 4 bachi hain. Total kitni moongphali?
hints: Where did the tens stop?
Count the leftovers on from 30.
3 tens and 4 more make 34.

items.prompt_en: You guessed 40 shells. We counted 38. Was your guess close or far?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne 40 shells ka guess kiya. Ginne pe 38 nikle. Guess paas tha ya door?
hints: How far is 38 from 40?
Count up from 38 to 40.
38, 39, 40: that is ___ steps.
Only 2 away, so it was a close, good guess.

items.prompt_en: I am going to spread these 8 bangles out in a long line. Before I do it: will there be more bangles, fewer, or the same?
items.prompt_hi: Main in 8 chudiyon ko ek lambi line mein phaila dungi. Usse pehle batao: chudiyan zyada ho jayengi, kam, ya utni hi?
hints: Will I add or take away any bangle?
Moving things does not change how many.
If no bangle is added or removed, there are still ___.
Still 8. Spreading out only changes the space, not the number.

verified.note: Key correct. Hint leak: hints 2-3 ('moving things does not change how many', 'still ___') give the answer early.

items.prompt_en: A box has 50 laddoos. Ravi guessed 45. Sita guessed 90. Whose guess is better, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Ek dibbe mein 50 laddoo hain. Ravi ka guess 45 tha, Sita ka 90. Kiska guess better hai, aur kyun?
items.answer: Ravi's: 45 is much closer to 50 than 90 is
hints: Which guess is nearer to 50?
Think how far each guess is from 50.
45 is ___ away; 90 is much farther.
Ravi's guess is only 5 away; Sita's is 40 away. Ravi's is better.

items.prompt_en: Your guess was 20 and the real number was 22. Why is that still a good guess?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhara guess 20 tha aur asli number 22. Phir bhi yeh achha guess kyun hai?
items.answer: An estimate only needs to be close; 20 is just 2 away from 22
hints: Does a guess have to be exact?
Think about how near 20 is to 22.
22 and 20 are only ___ apart.
A good estimate is close, not exact. 20 is only 2 away from 22.

verified.solverAnswer: an estimate only needs to be close; 20 is 2 from 22

items.prompt_en: A mela stall has balloons tied in bunches of 10. There are 6 bunches and 3 single balloons. How many balloons?
items.prompt_hi: Mele mein ek stall pe gubbare 10-10 ke guchchhe mein bandhe hain. 6 guchchhe hain aur 3 akele gubbare. Kitne gubbare?
hints: How many balloons in one bunch?
Count bunches by 10s, then add the singles.
6 tens and 3 ones make 63.

items.prompt_en: About 10 people can sit on one bench at the railway station. There are 7 benches and all are full. About how many people are sitting?
items.prompt_hi: Station pe ek bench pe lagbhag 10 log baith sakte hain. 7 bench hain, sab bhare hue. Lagbhag kitne log baithe hain?
hints: About how many on one bench?
Count the benches by 10s.
Seven benches of about 10 is about 70 people.

items.prompt_en: I made 4 groups of 10 marbles, and 5 marbles were left. So I said 4 + 5 = 9 marbles. Am I right?
items.prompt_hi: Maine 10-10 kanchon ke 4 group banaye aur 5 kanche bache. Toh maine bola 4 + 5 = 9 kanche. Kya main sahi hoon?
hints: How many marbles are in one group?
Each group is 10, not 1.
4 groups of 10 is 40, and 5 more is 45, not 9.

items.prompt_en: We have 5 groups of 10 seeds and 2 extra seeds. Show it with ten-sticks and single beads, then say the number.
items.prompt_hi: Humare paas beej ke 10-10 wale 5 group hain aur 2 beej alag. Ise ten-stick aur akele moti se dikhao, phir number bolo.
hints: How many ten-sticks will you need?
One ten-stick for each group of 10.
5 tens and 2 ones is ___.
5 ten-sticks and 2 beads show 52.

items.prompt_en: Golu thinks a guess is wrong if it is not exact. Tell Golu what a good guess (an estimate) is, and how we can check it.
items.prompt_hi: Golu sochta hai ki guess exact na ho toh galat hai. Golu ko batao achha guess (estimate) kya hota hai, aur use kaise check karte hain.
items.answer: An estimate is a thinking guess made without counting each one; good if close, not exact; check by making groups of 10 and counting
hints: What would you tell Golu first?
Talk about close, and about checking.
A good guess is ___ to the real number, and we check by making groups of ___.
A good estimate is close, not exact. We check it by making tens and counting.

verified.solverAnswer: estimate = close thinking guess, not exact; check by making tens

items.prompt_en: Remember from last time: what is an estimate?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad hai pichhli baar? Estimate kya hota hai?
items.answer: A thinking guess of how many, close to the real number, made without counting every one
hints: What do we do when we estimate?
It is a kind of guess.
An estimate is a guess that is ___ to the real number.
An estimate is a thinking guess that is close, made without counting each one.

verified.solverAnswer: a close, smart guess without counting each

items.prompt_en: There are 3 full bags of 10 rotis and a few more rotis on the plate. Before counting: will the total be more than 30 or less than 30?
items.prompt_hi: 10-10 roti ke 3 bhare thaile hain aur plate pe kuch roti aur. Ginne se pehle batao: total 30 se zyada hoga ya kam?
hints: How many rotis are in the 3 bags?
The bags make 30, and then there are some extra.
30 and a few more is ___ than 30.
Three bags make 30, and the extra rotis make it more than 30.

workedExample.problem: Guess how many marbles are in a heap, then check.
steps: Take out 10 marbles to see what 10 looks like.
The heap looks like about 4 of those groups, so guess about 40.
Check: make groups of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, and 3 are left.
Count on: 41, 42, 43. There are 43.
40 is close to 43, so it was a good estimate.
fadedVersion: Take out ___ marbles to see what 10 looks like.
The heap looks like about 4 groups, so guess about ___.
Check: make groups of 10: 10, 20, ___, 40, and 3 are left.
Count on: 41, 42, ___. There are 43.
40 is ___ to 43, so it was a good estimate.

skills.title: Name cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere
Match everyday objects to their 3D shape
Recognise a 3D shape in any position or size

expectations: Sphere: round all over, like a ball
Cube: all faces are the same squares, like a dice; cuboid: box with rectangle faces, like a matchbox
Cylinder: two flat circles and a curved side, like a gas cylinder
Cone: one flat circle and a point, like an ice-cream cone
Turning, moving or resizing an object does not change its shape name

misconceptions.belief: Thinks a cylinder lying down is a different shape from one standing up
signs: Gives a new name when the object is turned
Says a lying cylinder is a "roller", not a cylinder
Only recognises shapes in their usual position

diagnostic.prompt_en: A gas cylinder is standing. Then it is laid down on the floor. What shape is it now?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek gas cylinder khada hai. Phir use zameen pe lita diya. Ab woh kaunsi shape hai?

remediation.representation: A 3D viewer the child can rotate, with the name label staying fixed
remediation.moveShape: Child turns the object around and checks the faces each time; ask what changed and what stayed the same

misconceptions.belief: Names a 3D object by the flat shape of its face (calls a ball a circle, a dice a square)
signs: Says "circle" for a ball or laddoo
Says "square" for a dice
Cannot say how a roti and a laddoo differ

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is a ball a circle or a sphere?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ball circle hai ya sphere?

remediation.representation: Side by side: a flat roti and a round laddoo; let the child try to "hold" the circle drawn on paper
remediation.moveShape: Ask: can you hold it all around? Flat shapes are drawn on paper; solid shapes we can hold

misconceptions.belief: Calls every box a cube; does not see that a cube has all faces the same size
signs: Calls a matchbox or brick a cube
Says a dice and a matchbox are the same shape

diagnostic.prompt_en: Here is a dice and a matchbox. Which one is a cube?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Yeh rahe ek dice aur ek maachis ki dibbi. Inme se cube kaunsa hai?

remediation.representation: Unfold (net view) a dice and a matchbox and lay the faces next to each other
remediation.moveShape: Child compares face sizes; ask whether all faces are the same

items.prompt_en: A ball is round all over. What do we call this shape?
items.prompt_hi: Ball chaaron taraf se gol hoti hai. Is shape ko kya kehte hain?
hints: Think of the shape of a laddoo too.
It is a solid round shape, not a flat circle.
It starts with "sph…".
A ball is a sphere.

verified.note: Key correct. Hint leak: hint 3 ('starts with sph...') reveals the word.

items.prompt_en: Which shape is an ice-cream cone: a cone or a cylinder?
items.prompt_hi: Ice-cream cone kaunsi shape hai: cone ya cylinder?
hints: Does it have a pointed end?
A cylinder has two flat ends; this has one point.
One flat circle and a point is a ___.
An ice-cream cone is a cone.

items.prompt_en: Is a matchbox a cube or a cuboid?
items.prompt_hi: Maachis ki dibbi cube hai ya cuboid?
hints: Are all its faces the same size?
A cube has all faces the same; a matchbox is longer one way.
A box with rectangle faces is a ___.
A matchbox is a cuboid.

items.prompt_en: Look at a dice and a brick. How are they different? Which one is a cube?
items.prompt_hi: Ek dice aur ek eent dekho. Dono mein kya farak hai? Cube kaunsa hai?
items.answer: The dice is a cube (all faces are equal squares); the brick is a cuboid (longer, with rectangle faces)
hints: Look at the faces of each.
Check if every face is the same size.
The dice has all faces the ___.
The dice has all faces the same, so it is a cube. The brick is a cuboid.

verified.solverAnswer: dice is the cube (equal faces); brick is a cuboid

items.prompt_en: This battery cell is standing up. If I lay it down on its side, will it still be a cylinder?
items.prompt_hi: Yeh battery khadi hai. Agar main ise lita doon, toh kya yeh tab bhi cylinder rahegi?
hints: What will change when I lay it down?
Its faces stay the same: two flat circles and a curved side.
Turning it does not change its ___.
Yes. Lying or standing, it is still a cylinder.

verified.note: Key correct. Hint leak: hints 2-3 ('faces stay the same', 'turning does not change its ___') give 'yes' early.

items.prompt_en: Why is a cylinder still a cylinder when it is lying down?
items.prompt_hi: Cylinder let jaaye toh bhi woh cylinder kyun rehta hai?
items.answer: Turning it does not change its faces: it still has two flat circles and a curved side
hints: What makes a cylinder a cylinder?
Think about its faces.
It still has two flat ___ and one curved side.
Its faces do not change when it turns, so it is still a cylinder.

verified.solverAnswer: turning does not change faces: 2 flat circles + curved side

items.prompt_en: What shape is a laddoo?
items.prompt_hi: Laddoo kaunsi shape ka hota hai?
hints: Is it round all over?
Like a ball.
Round all over is a ___.
A laddoo is a sphere.

items.prompt_en: What shape is a birthday party cap?
items.prompt_hi: Birthday party wali topi kaunsi shape ki hoti hai?
hints: Does it have a point?
One round open end and a point at the top.
Like an ice-cream cone, it is a ___.
A party cap is a cone.

verified.note: Key correct. Hint leak: hint 3 ('Like an ice-cream cone, it is a ___') names the answer.

items.prompt_en: I am holding a football. I say: this is a circle! Is that right?
items.prompt_hi: Maine football pakdi hai. Main kehti hoon: yeh circle hai! Kya yeh sahi hai?
items.answer: No, a football is a sphere; a circle is flat
hints: Can you hold a circle drawn on paper?
A circle is flat; a football is round all over.
A solid round ball is a ___.
No. A football is a sphere. A circle is a flat shape.

verified.solverAnswer: No, football is a sphere; circle is flat

items.prompt_en: I will describe a shape, and you name the shape and one thing at home like it: it has two flat circle faces and one curved side.
items.prompt_hi: Main ek shape batati hoon, tum uska naam aur ghar ki ek cheez batao: iske do chapte gol face hain aur ek mudi hui side.
items.answer: Cylinder, for example a gas cylinder, a battery or a candle
hints: Which shape has two flat ends?
It can roll and also stand.
Two circles and a curved side is a ___.
It is a cylinder, like a gas cylinder or a battery.

verified.note: Open-ended naming: any cylinder-like object accepted; key examples correct.

items.prompt_en: In your kitchen, find one thing shaped like a cylinder, one like a cuboid and one like a sphere.
items.prompt_hi: Apni kitchen mein ek cylinder jaisi, ek cuboid jaisi aur ek sphere jaisi cheez dhoondo.
items.answer: Any correct objects, e.g. cylinder: steel dabba or gas cylinder; cuboid: masala box or biscuit packet; sphere: an orange or a lemon
hints: What round things are in the kitchen?
A sphere is round all over; a cuboid is a box; a cylinder is like a dabba.
A biscuit packet is a ___.
For example: a steel dabba is a cylinder, a biscuit packet is a cuboid, an orange is a sphere.

verified.solverAnswer: any valid: cylinder dabba, cuboid box/packet, sphere orange
verified.note: Open-ended: any correct kitchen objects are fine; solver confirms key examples.

items.prompt_en: Golu mixes up a cube and a cuboid. Explain the difference to Golu.
items.prompt_hi: Golu cube aur cuboid mein confuse ho jaata hai. Golu ko dono ka farak samjhao.
items.answer: A cube has all faces the same size (like a dice); a cuboid has rectangle faces and is longer one way (like a matchbox)
hints: What example of a cube could you show Golu?
Talk about the faces.
A cube has all faces the ___; a cuboid is ___ one way.
A cube, like a dice, has all faces the same. A cuboid, like a matchbox, has longer rectangle faces.

verified.solverAnswer: cube has all faces same; cuboid is longer one way

items.prompt_en: Which shape looks like a dice?
items.prompt_hi: Dice kis shape jaisi dikhti hai?
hints: Think about its faces.
All its faces are the same squares.

4 lines and 1 more.
A bundle shows 5.

skills.title: Read how many each row of a pictograph shows (one picture for one thing)
Compare rows: most, least and how many more
Make a simple pictograph from data

expectations: In this pictograph, one picture stands for one thing
Count the pictures in a row to find how many
Compare by counting, not by how big or long the row looks
"How many more" means find the difference: bigger number take away smaller number
When making one, use the same size pictures and line them up

misconceptions.belief: Thinks the row with bigger pictures (or a longer row) has more items
signs: Chooses the longer-looking row without counting
Says the bus row has more because buses are big pictures

diagnostic.prompt_en: Row A has 5 small car pictures. Row B has 4 big bus pictures, and it looks longer. Which row shows more vehicles?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Row A mein 5 chhoti car ki tasveerein hain. Row B mein 4 badi bus ki tasveerein, aur woh lambi dikhti hai. Kaunsi row zyada gaadiyan dikhati hai?

options.text: Row B, because it looks longer

remediation.representation: The same data redrawn with all pictures the same size and lined up in columns
remediation.moveShape: Child counts each row and then matches pictures one-to-one across rows

misconceptions.belief: When asked "how many more", gives the bigger number or adds the two numbers instead of finding the difference
signs: Says "7" for how many more cars (7) than buses (4)
Adds the rows: says 11
Does not match rows one-to-one

diagnostic.prompt_en: Cars: 7. Buses: 4. How many more cars than buses?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Car: 7. Bus: 4. Bus se kitni zyada car hain?

remediation.moveShape: Child pairs each bus with a car and counts the cars left without a partner

items.prompt_en: In the pictograph, the cycle row has 6 cycle pictures. How many cycles passed the school gate?
items.prompt_hi: Pictograph mein cycle wali row mein 6 cycle ki tasveerein hain. School gate se kitni cycle guzri?
hints: What does one picture stand for?
One picture is one cycle.
Count the pictures: ___.
6 pictures means 6 cycles.

items.prompt_en: A pictograph shows cars 5, autos 8 and buses 2. Which vehicle passed the most?
items.prompt_hi: Ek pictograph mein car 5, auto 8 aur bus 2 hain. Sabse zyada kaunsi gaadi guzri?
hints: Which number is the biggest?
Compare 5, 8 and 2.
The biggest is ___.
Autos passed the most: 8.

items.prompt_en: In the same pictograph (cars 5, autos 8, buses 2), which passed the least?
items.prompt_hi: Usi pictograph mein (car 5, auto 8, bus 2), sabse kam kaunsi guzri?
hints: Which number is the smallest?
Compare 5, 8 and 2.
The smallest is ___.
Buses passed the least: 2.

items.prompt_en: Autos: 8, cars: 5. How many more autos than cars?
items.prompt_hi: Auto: 8, car: 5. Car se kitne zyada auto hain?
hints: Pair each car with an auto. How many autos have no partner?
Find the difference: 8 − 5.
3 more autos than cars.

items.prompt_en: One row has 4 big elephant pictures. Another has 6 small rabbit pictures. The elephant row looks longer. Guess first: which row has more animals?
items.prompt_hi: Ek row mein 4 bade haathi ki tasveerein hain. Doosri mein 6 chhote khargosh ki. Haathi wali row lambi dikhti hai. Pehle guess karo: kis row mein zyada jaanwar hain?
items.answer: The rabbit row: 6 is more than 4
hints: Count each row.
Big pictures do not mean more.
6 is more than ___.
The rabbit row has more: 6 rabbits and only 4 elephants.

items.prompt_en: Two pictographs show the same data. One uses big pictures and one uses small pictures. Do the answers change?
items.prompt_hi: Do pictograph ek hi data dikhate hain. Ek mein badi tasveerein hain, ek mein chhoti. Kya jawab badalte hain?
items.answer: No: the counts are the same, so the answers are the same
hints: Does the number of pictures change?
We count pictures, not their size.
The counts stay the ___.
No. The number of pictures is the same, so the answers do not change.

items.prompt_en: Why should every picture in a pictograph be the same size and lined up?
items.prompt_hi: Pictograph mein har tasveer ek hi size ki aur line mein kyun honi chahiye?
items.answer: So that a longer row really means more; different sizes could trick us into thinking a row has more
hints: What could a big picture make us think?
Same size helps us compare by looking.
Same size and lined up so longer means ___.
With same-size pictures lined up, a longer row really means more. Big pictures could trick us.

verified.solverAnswer: so we are not tricked by size

items.prompt_en: A favourite-sweet pictograph shows jalebi 7, laddoo 4 and rasgulla 5. How many children were asked in all?
items.prompt_hi: Pasandida mithai ke pictograph mein jalebi 7, laddoo 4 aur rasgulla 5 hain. Kul kitne bachchon se poochha gaya?
hints: What do we do to find "in all"?
Add all three rows.
7 + 4 + 5 = 16 children.

items.prompt_en: Jalebi has 7 pictures and laddoo has 4. The question is: how many more children chose jalebi? I said 11. Check me.
items.prompt_hi: Jalebi ki 7 tasveerein aur laddoo ki 4. Sawaal: kitne zyada bachchon ne jalebi chuni? Maine kaha 11. Check karo.
items.answer: No: it is 3 (11 is the total)
hints: Did I add or find the difference?
"How many more" means the difference.
No. 11 is the total. How many more is 7 − 4 = 3.

items.prompt_en: Make a pictograph: 3 children came by bus, 5 walked and 2 came by auto. How many pictures go in each row?
items.prompt_hi: Ek pictograph banao: 3 bachche bus se aaye, 5 paidal aur 2 auto se. Har row mein kitni tasveerein lagengi?
hints: One picture stands for how many children?
One picture for each child.
Bus row: ___ pictures.
Bus 3 pictures, walk 5 pictures, auto 2 pictures.

items.prompt_en: A pictograph shows rainy days: June 8, July 12, August 10. Which month was the wettest? How many more rainy days were there in July than in June?
items.prompt_hi: Ek pictograph mein baarish ke din hain: June 8, July 12, August 10. Sabse zyada baarish kis mahine hui? June se July mein kitne zyada baarish ke din the?
hints: Which month has the most pictures?
Then find 12 − 8.
July was the wettest, with 4 more rainy days than June.

items.prompt_en: Teach Golu how to read a pictograph.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao ki pictograph kaise padhte hain.
items.answer: Find what one picture stands for, count the pictures in each row, and compare the counts, not the size of the pictures
hints: What should Golu check first?
Talk about counting and comparing.
One picture is ___ thing; count each ___.
Check what one picture means, count each row, then compare the numbers.

verified.solverAnswer: what one picture means, count rows, compare

items.prompt_en: One row has 9 pictures and another has 6. How many more are in the first row?
items.prompt_hi: Ek row mein 9 tasveerein hain aur doosri mein 6. Pehli row mein kitni zyada hain?
hints: How many more means what?
Find the difference.
3 more in the first row.

workedExample.problem: Pictograph: cars 7, buses 4. How many more cars than buses?
steps: Count the car row: 7. Count the bus row: 4.
Match each bus with a car.
3 cars have no bus partner.
So there are 3 more cars than buses (7 − 4 = 3).
